label: L9 · Cocci: What the Lecturer Flagged
rows: ★ Yellow highlights
The deck's 14 yellow-highlighted passages are her emphasis (“I tried to highlight some things”). Starred rows below.
★ M-protein
“This M protein, which you might also want to highlight”: M-protein → resistance to PHAGOCYTOSIS (Streptococcus pyogenes).
★ Lancefield A and B
“The A and the B are the primo ones.” Group A = Streptococcus pyogenes; group B = Streptococcus agalactiae.
Not to memorize

“Don't worry about digging down into the Lancefield letters”: the minor groups (C, G and the letters in the slide 26 table) · the rate maps and STD (sexually transmitted disease) graphs, slides 62–66.

label: L9 · The Gram-Positive Decision Tree
rows: ★ Gram stain
Gram-positive = THICK peptidoglycan = physically strong. Gram-negative = thin = chemically strong. Staph = irregular CLUSTERS; strep = CHAINS.
★ Staph always
Non-spore-forming and non-motile (no spores, no flagella); may have capsules.
★ Catalase
Hydrogen peroxide: bubbles = staphylococci (+). No bubbles = streptococci and enterococci (−).
Coagulase
Coagulase + = Staphylococcus aureus (97% of isolates; the diagnostic trait). Coagulase − = the other staphylococci.
★ Hemolysis
Blood agar detects hemolysis. BETA = complete, clear zone (A, B, C, G, some D). ALPHA = partial, GREEN (pneumococcus, viridans).
Bacitracin / optochin
Beta + bacitracin SENSITIVE = group A (Streptococcus pyogenes); resistant = B, C. Alpha + optochin SENSITIVE = Streptococcus pneumoniae; resistant = D, viridans.
Salt
Staphylococcus aureus withstands high salinity (mannitol salts agar). Streptococci grow poorly on it — too saline.

label: L9 · Staphylococci
rows: Staphylococcus aureus
Golden (“aureus”) colonies, 37°C, FACULTATIVE anaerobe; tolerates salt, pH, heat. Carried in the ANTERIOR NARES (20–60% of adults).
Enzymes
Coagulase clots plasma · staphylokinase digests clots · hyaluronidase digests connective tissue · lipases aid skin colonization · penicillinase inactivates penicillin.
Toxins

Hemolysins lyse red cells · LEUKOCIDIN lyses neutrophils and macrophages · ENTEROTOXIN = gut distress · EXFOLIATIVE separates epidermis from dermis · TSST (toxic shock syndrome toxin) = fever, vomiting, shock.
Skin
Folliculitis (follicle) → FURUNCLE (boil, abscess) → CARBUNCLE (cluster of joined furuncles). Impetigo: bubble-like swellings that break and peel.
Systemic & toxigenic
Osteomyelitis in the METAPHYSIS · bacteremia from another site or a DEVICE (endocarditis risk) · food intoxication = HEAT-STABLE enterotoxin · scalded skin · toxic shock (classically tampons).
Treatment & prevention

95% make penicillinase. Methicillin-resistant strains: multiple resistance, now COMMUNITY acquired too; some resist all but VANCOMYCIN. Abscess = surgical drainage. Universal precautions; don't share towels, razors.
Coagulase-negative

Nosocomial, opportunistic, start polymicrobial BIOFILMS. Epidermidis: skin, mucosa → endocarditis, bacteremia, UTI (urinary tract infection). Hominis: apocrine (lipid-rich) armpit and groin. Capitis: scalp, face, ear. All three: wound infection via broken skin. Saprophyticus: may cause UTI.

label: L9 · Streptococci & Enterococci
rows: General
Chains, facultative anaerobes, FASTIDIOUS (enriched media), sensitive to drying, heat, disinfectants. Lancefield = cell wall C-CARBOHYDRATE antigens (Rebecca Lancefield, 1933).
★ Group A virulence

C-carbohydrate vs lysozyme · fimbriae adhere · M-PROTEIN vs phagocytosis · hyaluronic acid capsule = no immune response · C5a protease blocks complement · streptolysins O, S = hemolysins · erythrogenic toxin = fever + rash · superantigens · streptokinase digests fibrin.
★ Group A spread
STRICTLY human; humans the only reservoir. Contact, droplets, food, fomites; portal skin or pharynx; mostly CHILDREN.
Group A disease
Impetigo = contagious CRUST, schoolchildren · erysipelas = into dermis and subcutaneous tissue · pharyngitis · scarlet fever = PROPHAGE for erythrogenic toxin · septicemia, pneumonia, toxic shock.
Group A sequelae
Rheumatic fever after pharyngitis → valve damage, arthritis, chorea. Acute glomerulonephritis → nephritis, high blood pressure, kidney failure.
★ Group B

Streptococcus agalactiae: vagina, pharynx, large intestine. Reaches the infant during VAGINAL DELIVERY → top cause of neonatal pneumonia, sepsis, meningitis. SCREEN and treat pregnant women (intravenous penicillin in practice; slide's streptomycin is wrong).
Enterococci (group D)
Separated from Streptococcus by 16S ribosomal RNA (1984). Large intestine; urinary, wound, skin infection in the debilitated; MULTIPLE antibiotics.
Identification
Rapid tests = monoclonal antibody to C-carbohydrate. Culture: bacitracin, CAMP, bile esculin. CAMP factor + beta-hemolytic Staphylococcus aureus = FLAME or ARROW; also detects Listeria.
Treatment
Groups A and B: PENICILLIN. Long-term penicillin after rheumatic fever or recurrent strep throat. ★ Big problems with resistant strains.

label: L9 · Viridans Streptococci & the Pneumococcus
rows: ★ Viridans
Most numerous in gums, teeth, mouth. Not very invasive: DENTAL or SURGICAL procedures let them in. Worst = SUBACUTE ENDOCARDITIS (pre-existing heart disease).
Streptococcus mutans
Slime layers on teeth → PLAQUE and caries. Dental prophylaxis now only for certain heart conditions.
Pneumococcus: lab
LANCET-shaped pairs and short chains · blood or chocolate agar · CAPNOPHILIC (5–10% carbon dioxide) · lacks catalase AND peroxidase, dies in high lab oxygen.
Pneumococcus: disease
Large CAPSULE = main virulence factor (types vary). Pneumonia by ASPIRATION; otitis media via the EUSTACHIAN TUBE. Endogenous; very young, elderly, compromised, crowded.
Pneumococcus: treatment
Penicillin, but rising resistance. Conjugate vaccine for children 2–23 months; capsular vaccine for older adults (adults now also get conjugate vaccines).

label: L9 · Neisseria, Moraxella & Acinetobacter
rows: Neisseria
Gram-negative BEAN-shaped DIPLOCOCCI, thin peptidoglycan, no flagella or spores, PILI attach. Strict human parasites. Microaerophilic. Catalase + and cytochrome OXIDASE +.
★ Culture
Chocolate agar in a CANDLE JAR = enhanced carbon dioxide (not an anaerobic culture).
Gonococcus

Fimbriae · IgA protease (immunoglobulin A). Dose 100–1,000 cells; 1–2 hours on fomites. Asymptomatic: 50% of females, 10% of males. Salpingitis → sterility, ectopic pregnancy. Arthritis, conjunctivitis, pharyngitis.
Gonococcus: diagnosis

Gram-negative diplococci INSIDE NEUTROPHILS = presumptive. Penicillinase-producing and tetracycline-resistant strains. No lasting immunity → recurs. Reportable. Newborn eyes: topical antibiotics at birth.
Meningococcus
Capsule, fimbriae, IgA protease, ENDOTOXIN (hemorrhage, shock). Nasopharynx; close quarters, DORMS; 6 months–3 years and 10–20 years. Blood → blood-brain barrier → cerebrospinal fluid.
Meningococcus: care
Culture slow → rapid capsular polysaccharide tests. Intravenous penicillin G or cephalosporin; prophylaxis for CLOSE CONTACTS; vaccine = purified capsular antigens.
Moraxella
Branhamella catarrhalis, RECLASSIFIED into Moraxella; nasopharynx; opportunist in cancer, diabetic, alcoholic patients.
★ Acinetobacter
Acinetobacter baumannii: multidrug-resistant COCCOBACILLI, hospital acquired, especially in MILITARY hospitals. (The genus lives in soil; this species is a hospital organism.)
